argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean no-caveat certification, but it does support certification on a caveated basis. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.4 percentage points and the launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports overall launch readiness. The same admissible record also shows a remaining below-target field-service dispatch issue in technician safety-note routing, a draft-only mitigation runbook with TBD owner and threshold, and a model-card draft that is not yet aligned with that limitation. The supportable certification position is therefore narrow: certify only with explicit disclosure of the unresolved limitation in the packet and model-card record, not as a claim that no material limitation exists or that draft monitoring closes the gap.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit question. The narrow request is to avoid unnecessary escalation by aligning the verdict to what the admissible evidence actually supports: certification with caveats rather than a broader noncompliance conclusion.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy text is the limiting condition here. It states that certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show either condition is met. It also states that draft runbooks, dashboards, and future monitoring can support risk management but do not remove a current disclosure requirement unless approved. On that record, the policy-consistent position is caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure of the unresolved launch-use-case limitation.
concessions: The record does not support certification without material caveats.
The draft mitigation runbook is not an approved mitigation because the owner and alert threshold remain TBD.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves satisfy the policy standard for clean certification.
The current model-card draft is inconsistent with the unresolved limitation unless it is updated to disclose that limitation for the named launch use case.
